evidenceRegister.text: Board committees with climate-related responsibilities. The Board discharges its responsibility for oversight of climate strategy and climate-related risks and opportunities with the assistance of three standing committees.

Chief Commercial and Sustainability Officer oversees climate reporting and strategy. Table 5 summarises the Group's total absolute gross greenhouse gas emissions for FY26, comprising Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions.
The role of the Board. The Board provides leadership and approves the strategic direction and objectives of the Group.
Board skills and experience. Sustainability and Environment: Expertise in managing and driving environmental management and social responsibility initiatives and reporting.
Table 3: FY26 Performance measures for the MD & CEO. Sustainability 10% target weighting, Threshold Achieved, 5.0% actual STI outcome.
External and strategic risks. Climate change and environment: Coles has a responsibility to reduce the effect of our operations on the environment.

Sustainability Report prepared in accordance with Australian Sustainability Reporting Standards. As this is the first year in which the Group has applied AASB S2, the Group has elected to apply the transition relief to not disclose comparative information.
Business model. Coles is one of Australia's leading retailers. Our value chain diagram illustrates the key interactions across suppliers, operations and customers.
The CRRO assessment process is iterative: initial identification, validation and assessment, mitigation and response, and prioritisation, identifying six climate-related risks and one opportunity.
Climate scenario analysis using low-warming and high-warming scenarios: Sustainability - Paris aligned, Middle of the road, Fossil-fuelled development, modelled by ClimSystems.
Scenario assumptions underpinning anticipated climate-related effects, informed by SSP2-4.5. The Group identified seven CRROs and deployed approximately $112 million of capital expenditure.
Transition risk: Energy system volatility, rising prices and supply disruptions. No material impact on the Group in FY26.
Transition risk: Changing policy, regulatory and legal requirements to decarbonise and manage climate risk, including a potential carbon price.
Transition risk: Dependency on our third-party suppliers and logistics partners to reduce emissions and adopt low-carbon practices.
Transition risk: Delayed adoption of low-emissions technology, including conversion of refrigeration and HVAC assets. Capital expenditure of $109 million incurred in FY26.
Physical risk: Risk to the growth and/or production of agricultural raw materials due to extreme weather events and climate conditions.
Physical risk: Risk to the resilience of our store and supply chain operations due to extreme weather events and climate conditions.
Opportunity: Offering more sustainable products to customers to meet changing customer preferences, such as plant-based protein alternatives.
Climate resilience: the Group's strategy and business model are expected to remain broadly resilient under both low- and high-warming scenarios.
Response to climate-related transition risks and opportunities under the low-warming scenario: reducing Scope 1 and 2 emissions through 100% renewable electricity.
Response to physical climate-related risks under the high-warming scenario: enhancing resilience of the agricultural supply base and operational footprint.
Transition planning and our Climate Transition Plan, released August 2026, sets out strategic approach to supporting lower-emissions and more resilient food systems.
Impairment of non-financial assets: climate-related risks and opportunities were considered in assessing recoverable amounts of the Group's CGUs, with no material impact identified.
Coles risk management process, supported by three lines of accountability, based on ISO 31000: Risk Management Guidelines.
Approach to risk management: Coles conducts an annual CRRO assessment. The Board oversees the Group's approach to identifying, assessing and managing CRROs.

Cross-industry metrics: physical and transition risk exposure by site count and percentage. Capital deployment of $112m towards climate-related risks and opportunities, plus an internal carbon price schedule.
Climate-related target: Deliver net zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions by 2050, with an interim FY30 target of >=75% reduction from FY20 baseline, validated by SBTi.
During FY26 the Group achieved an 82.6% reduction in combined Scope 1 and 2 market-based emissions relative to FY20. FLAG target: 30.3% reduction by end of FY30.
Scope 3 supplier engagement target: 80% of suppliers by spend to have science-based emissions reduction targets by end of FY29. 46.9% achieved as at end of FY26.

Basis of preparation, judgements and assumptions for emissions measurement. Scope 1 and 2 emissions measured using NGER methods; Scope 3 estimated using spend-based methodologies where activity data unavailable.
Table 9: Measurement approach, inputs and emissions factors for Scope 1 and 2 emissions reporting, sourced from the Australian National Greenhouse Accounts Factors 2025.
Table 10: Measurement approach, emissions factors, inputs and assumptions for material Scope 3 categories, including data quality notes and limitations.
Contractual instruments: LGC agreements with clean energy generators and retailers. Directors' Declaration confirming compliance with AASB S2 and the Corporations Act.
Independent auditor's report to the members of Coles Group Limited: review and audit conclusions on selective sustainability information under ASSA 5010 and ASSA 5000.

Inherent limitations: climate-related risk management is an emerging area using developing and uncertain data and methodologies; GHG emissions quantification is subject to significant measurement uncertainty.
